name: Thiruvallikkeni (Triplicane)
significance: The charioteer of Arjuna in the heart of Chennai — Vishnu here bears the scars of the Mahabharata arrows.

name: Thiruneermalai
significance: The hill where the Lord gave darshan in four forms — standing, seated, reclining and walking — in one complex.

name: Thirukkachi (Kanchipuram — Atthigiri)
significance: The Lord of Hastigiri hill — the boon-granting Varadaraja, whose Athi-varadar emerges once in forty years.

name: Thiruvekkaa
significance: The Lord who obeyed his devotee Thirumazhisai Azhwar’s word and shifted the shrine — "as told, so done".

name: Ashtabujagaram
significance: The eight-armed Vishnu who quelled the arrogance of the demons with his many weapons.

name: Thiruooragam (Ulagalantha Perumal)
significance: The colossus of Vamana’s three strides — one foot raised to measure the very universe.

name: Thiruneeragam
significance: The water-form Lord within the Ulagalantha temple — worshipped as Neeragam, the essence of the sacred waters.

name: Thirukkaragam
significance: The ocean of mercy (Karunakara) housed within the Ulagalantha Perumal temple complex.

name: Thirukkaarvaanam
significance: The cloud-hued Lord of the sacred grove, within the Ulagalantha temple complex of Kanchi.

name: Thiru Parameswara Vinnagaram
significance: The three-tiered Pallava masterpiece where Vishnu is seated, reclining and standing — one above the other.

name: Thiruppaavalavannam
significance: The coral-hued Lord who appeared from the fire of the sacrificial rites of the sages.

name: Thiruppadagam
significance: Krishna seated in his giant form as the messenger (thoodhar) of the Pandavas before the great war.

name: Thiru Nilathingal Thundam
significance: Vishnu worshipped inside Shiva’s Ekambaranathar temple — the "quarter of the moon-hued gem".

name: Thirukkalvanoor
temple: Sri Aadhi Varaha Perumal Shrine (Kamakshi Amman complex)
significance: The primordial Varaha hidden within the Kamakshi Amman temple — the "thief" who steals hearts.

name: Thiruvelukkai
significance: The Lion-man seated in yoga on the hill of the divine horses, guarding his devotees in fierce love.

name: Thiruthanka
significance: The Lord of light — the lamp that dispelled the darkness after the deluge; Poigai Azhwar’s beloved shrine.

name: Thirupputkuzhi
significance: Where Rama performed the last rites for the eagle Jatayu — the Lord holding the bird in tender devotion.

name: Thiruvallur (Veeraraghava)
significance: The divine physician — the Lord reclines on his serpent bed here healing the ills of his devotees.

name: Thirunindravur
significance: The Lord who was delayed by his devotee’s love and stayed at Nindravur on his way to Tirupati.

name: Thiruvidanthai
significance: The ever-wedding Lord by the sea who married 360 nymphs in a single day, holding them all as one.

name: Thirukkadalmallai
significance: The Lord reclines on the shore floor at the Pallava port town — birthplace of Bhoothathazhwar.

name: Thirukkadigai (Sholinghur)
significance: The yoga-seated Narasimha on the hill — where seven rishins are said to be in eternal meditation even now.

name: Srirangam
significance: The foremost of all 108 Divya Desams — the huge island temple of Lord Ranganatha reclining on Adisesha, sung by eleven of the twelve Azhwars.

name: Thirukkozhi (Uraiyur)
significance: Ancient Chola capital where the Lord appears as the beautiful bridegroom of Kamalavalli Nachiyar.

name: Thirukkarambanoor (Uthamar Kovil)
significance: One of the rare shrines where the Trimurtis are worshipped together; Vishnu grants the Purushothama blessing here.

name: Thiruvellarai
significance: A hill temple older than Srirangam according to tradition, with the rare shrine of Lord in white and dark forms.

name: Thiru Anbil
significance: The Lord reclines here facing the Kollidam river, worshipped by sage Valmiki according to tradition.

name: Thirupper Nagar (Koviladi)
significance: The Lord reclines holding a pot of nectar (appam), blessing Emperor Sibhi according to the sthala purana.

name: Thirukkandiyur
temple: Sri Hara Saabha Vimochana Perumal Temple
significance: Where Shiva was freed from his curse after the Brahma-slaying episode, uniting Vaishnavism and Shaivism in one shrine.

name: Thiruvelliyangudi
significance: Lord Rama appears here with his bow, in a rare form granting the vision of the Kalyana Ramar.

name: Thiru Aadhanoor
significance: The Lord reclines on Adisesha measuring the ages of time, guarding the cosmic wheel of the year.

name: Thirukkudanthai (Kumbakonam)
significance: One of the Pancharanga kshetras; the Lord reclines here rising slightly to hear Thirumazhisai Azhwar’s plea.

name: Thiruppullam Boothangudi
significance: Lord Rama stands with bow in hand as the hunter-archer who descended for Maricha’s deliverance.

name: Thirukkavithalam (Kabisthalam)
significance: Where Lord Vishnu hurried to rescue the elephant Gajendra from the crocodile — the emblem of divine grace.

name: Thirunandhipura Vinnagaram
significance: Worshipping here is said to equal the fruit of worshipping at Tirupati, according to the Azhwar’s hymns.
mapQuery: Jagannatha Perumal Temple Nathan Koil Thanjavur

name: Thirukkoodalur (Aduthurai)
significance: Where the Lord protected the Devas who gathered (koodal) in assembly and rescued the elephant of Indra.

name: Thiruvinnagar
significance: The Lord who accepted food without salt from his consort Bhoomidevi — "Uppu illa appan" — granting boons without question.

name: Thirunaraiyur (Nachiyar Kovil)
significance: The only kshetram where the Goddess leads the worship — the Nachiyar is given first honours in all rituals.

name: Thirucherai
significance: The Lord with five consorts who preserved the Vedas and seeds of creation at the end of the deluge.

name: Thirukkannamangai
significance: The Lord consumed the nectar of devotion of the sages — the "Abode of the Lord of Kannamangai".

name: Thanjai Mamanikoil
significance: Three adjacent shrines in Thanjavur — Neelamegha, Manikundran and Narasimhan — counted as one Divya Desam.

name: Thiruvazhundur
significance: Birthplace of the poet Kambar’s patron region; the Lord appears in regal glory as King of the Devas.

name: Thiruchirupuliyur
significance: Where the Lord blessed sage Vyagrapadar; the sanctum is said to have been built by divine hands overnight.

name: Thalaichangadu (Nanmathiyam)
significance: The Lord of the Chola-era Chola shrine where a conch was once gifted — the "head-conch" village.

name: Thiruindalur (Mayiladuthurai)
significance: The fragrant Ranganatha on the Cauvery’s northern bank, where the river itself is said to worship the Lord.

name: Thirukkannapuram
significance: Sowrirajan who grew a tuft of hair to honor his devotee’s word — renowned for instant grace.

name: Thirukkannankudi
significance: The Lord who tried to walk away with his devotee’s butter-offering — Damodara’s playful kshetram.

name: Thirunaagai (Nagapattinam)
significance: The beautiful (Soundara) Raja of the coastal town, praised by Thirumangai Azhwar in moving verses.

name: Chidambaram
temple: Sri Govindaraja Perumal Temple (in Natarajar complex)
significance: Lord Vishnu reclines within the famed Nataraja temple complex — the vision of Siva and Vishnu as one.

name: Thirukkannalangudi (Sirkazhi)
significance: Where Vamana measured the three worlds in one stride — the great Trivikrama shrine of the Kaveri delta.

name: Thiruvaaali – Thirunagari
significance: Two adjacent villages counted as one Desam — the seat of the pacified Lakshmi Narasimha.

name: Thirukavalampaadi
significance: Krishna of the cowherd settlement in the sacred Thirunangur cluster of eleven Desams.

name: Thiruarimeya Vinnagaram
significance: The Lord seated in the rare "pot-dance" posture (Kudam Koothan) of the Thirunangar group.

name: Thiruvanpurushothamam
significance: The Supreme Purusha who rode the chariot of the gods in the Mahabharata war, worshipped here.

name: Thirusemponseikoil
significance: The golden-gifted shrine — Rama is said to have worshipped here with gold for the slain Jatayu’s rites.

name: Thirumanimaadakoil
significance: The jewel-pavilion temple of the Thirunangur eleven, seated facing the devotee in royal audience.

name: Thiruvaikunta Vinnagaram
significance: The presiding deity of the Thirunangur festival — eleven Deities ride together in the famed Garuda seva.

name: Thirudevanaartogai
significance: Where the assembled Devas (deva-sangam) worshipped Vishnu — the leader of the divine host.

name: Thiruthetriyaambalam
significance: The reclining Ranganatha who raised his hand in blessing to the celestials — the sanctum of vows.

name: Thirumanikkoodam
significance: The boon-giving Varadaraja of the Thirunangur group, guardian of the jewel-hall.

name: Thiruvellakkulam (Annan Kovil)
significance: The "elder brother" (Annan) of Tirupati Srinivasa — a white-tank shrine equal in glory to Venkatam.

name: Thiruppaarththanpalli
significance: Where Arjuna (Parthan) is said to have worshipped — the Lord of the lotus-eyed one.

name: Thiruaheendrapuram
significance: The Lord of the Devas carried by Adisesha on the Aushada hill — sanctuary of Indra’s worship.

name: Thirukkoviloor
significance: Where the first three Azhwars were sheltered in a single lamp’s light — the Vamana kshetram of the Pennai river.

name: Thirukkurungudi
significance: The beautiful Nambi of the Mahendragiri foothills — where the Lord himself came as a disciple to Vaishnava teachers.

name: Thirucheeravaramangai (Nanguneri)
significance: The Lord seated on the Adisesha banyan (vanamamalai) — a great eternal lamp burns here without cease.

name: Azhwar Thirunagari
significance: The birthplace of Nammazhwar — the Lord himself is said to serve as the eternal disciple of the great saint.

name: Thirukkolur
significance: The Lord who "gives the truth of boons" — a young girl of this village, Pitchai, is celebrated in tradition.

name: Thirupper
significance: The Lord with fish-shaped earrings, adorning Varuna the rain god himself.

name: Thiruvaikundam (Srivaikuntam)
significance: Vaikunta on earth — the Lord reclines here on Adisesha having vanquished the demon for the Vedas.

name: Thirukkulandai (Perungulam)
significance: One of the Nava Thirupathi nine on the Thamirabarani — Srinivasa of the great tank village.

name: Thiruvaragunamangai
significance: The Lord seated in victory posture on the Garuda vahana — one of the Nava Thirupathi cluster.

name: Thiruppuliangudi
significance: The Lord who arrived with the fire of devotion — praised as the emitter of Kadir (light) in Nammazhwar’s hymns.

name: Thirutholaivillimangalam
significance: The twin temples (Irattai Thirupathi) counted as one Desam — the lotus-eyed Lord and Devapiran.

name: Thiruthangal
significance: Standing Narayana beside the great Saneeswara shrine — refuge of the Pandya country’s faithful.

name: Srivilliputhur
significance: Birthplace of Andal and Periyazhwar — the Lord reclines on the banyan leaf; the temple tower is Tamil Nadu’s emblem.

name: Thirukkoodal (Madurai)
significance: The assembly of rivers worships this Azhagar in the Pandya capital of Madurai, in three ascending postures.

name: Thirumaalirunsolai (Azhagar Kovil)
significance: The handsome Azhagar of the fragrant hills who rides to Madurai each Chithirai for the river goddess.

name: Thirumogur
significance: Home of the celebrated Chakkaram — the rare Sudarshana of Mogur with 154 hands radiating protection.

name: Thiruppullani (Darbasayana)
significance: Where Rama lay on darba grass for three days invoking the sea-king — the Adi Jagannatha shrine of the coast.

name: Thirukkotiyoor
significance: The ashtaanga-vimana where Ramanuja proclaimed the sacred names aloud to all — the Ashtakshara kshetram.

name: Thirumeyyam
significance: The hill-cave shrine of Sathya-moorthi — the Lord of Truth with his giant Anantasayana rock-cut reclining form.

name: Thiruvananthapuram
significance: The Lord reclines eternally on Anantha through three doors — the royal shrine of Travancore and its hidden treasures.

name: Thiruvanparisaram
significance: The Lord whose chest bears Sri — birthplace of the acharya Nathamuni’s lineage shrine of the Nanjil country.

name: Thirukkatkarai (Thrikkakara)
significance: The Vamana kshetram of Kerala — the origin of the Onam festival and the sacred Onappookkalam floral offering.

name: Thirumoozhikkalam
significance: Where Hema the sage’s serpent-curse was lifted — the Lord of the sacred mantra-clearing waters.

name: Thiruppuliyur
significance: The wonder-working Lord of the Chera heartland, worshipped by the sages of the Puliyur forest.

name: Thiruchengundrur (Chengannur)
significance: The hill-temple of the Devas — the railway-age gateway for pilgrims to Sabarimala’s Vishnu shrine.

name: Thirunavai
significance: On the banks of the Bharathapuzha where Kerala’s ritual offerings for ancestors (bali) are performed.

name: Thiruvallavazh (Thiruvalla)
significance: The great Vallabha temple with its famed flag-post of black stone — where Garuda himself is said to worship.

name: Thiruvanvandoor
significance: Built by the legendary architect Perunchithiran — the serpent-tank Lord of the Pamba river country.

name: Thiruvaranvilai (Aranmula)
significance: Famed for the Aranmula Parthasarathy boat race and the sacred metal mirrors made for the temple.

name: Thiruvattaru
significance: The Lord reclines between the rivers Para and Kothai — marble-inlaid Vishnu of the old Travancore country.

name: Thiruvithuvakkodu
significance: The refuge-granting (Abhayapradha) Lord of Kaladi’s neighbourhood — shield of the surrendered soul.

name: Thirukkodithanam
significance: Sahadeva of the Pandavas is said to have worshipped here — the "flag-planting" shrine of Kerala legend.

name: Thiruvengadam (Tirumala)
significance: The Lord of the Seven Hills — the most visited shrine in the world, sung as the boundless Venkata hill by the Azhwars.

name: Thirusingavel Kundram (Ahobilam)
significance: The cave-shrine of Ugra Narasimha in the Nallamala hills — nine forms of the Lion-man in one sacred forest.

name: Thiru Ayodhi
significance: The birth-city of Rama on the Sarayu — sung from afar by Thirumangai Azhwar who never left Tamil soil.

name: Thiru Naimisaranyam
significance: The forest where the Puranas were first narrated — Vishnu is present here as the forest itself.

name: Thiru Salagramam (Muktinath)
significance: The Himalayan shrine of the sacred saligrama stones — 108 waterspouts of liberation at 3,800 metres.

name: Thiruvadhari Ashramam (Badrinath)
significance: The Lord seated in yoga under the badri tree in the Garhwal Himalayas — the moksha-giving tapovan of the north.

name: Thirukkandam (Devaprayag)
significance: Where the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi merge to become the Ganga — Vishnu of the sacred confluence.

name: Thiruppirudhi (Joshimutt)
significance: The winter seat of Badrinath — where the deity of Badri is worshipped when the Himalayan shrine closes in snow.

name: Thiru Vadamathura
significance: The birth-city of Krishna on the Yamuna — where the Lord lifted Govardhana hill on his little finger.

name: Thiruaaypaadi
significance: The cowherd settlement of Krishna’s youth — the eternally enchanting Navamohana of the Azhwars’ longing.

name: Thiru Dwaraka
significance: Krishna’s golden city by the western sea — the gateway (dwaraka) city that the Arabian waters once swallowed.

name: Thiruppaarkadal
significance: The Ocean of Milk where Vishnu reclines on Ananta — a Divya Desam beyond earthly geography, reached in contemplation.

name: Thirupparamapadham
significance: The supreme abode Vaikuntam itself — the final destination of the liberated soul, the last of the 108.
